thread:
maya: Hey — seeing a weird latency spike on H100 pool after yesterday's driver bump (535 -> 544). Tail for 512-seqlen requests shows kernel path flipping mid-request. Anyone else?

jin: yup, noticed on prod-canary metrics around 11:30 UTC. p50 is fine but p99 increased ~28ms and cost per-token drifted.

sam: can you paste the profiler snippet?

maya: pasted a quick profiler snapshot from a problematic trace:
```text
kernel_choice: aten_attn_optimized_v2
seq_len: 512
kv_cache_mode: enabled
batch_bucket: 8-12
latency_tokens: 12.3ms
fallbacks: 0 -> switched to aten_attn_generic mid-seq
```

jin: autotuner history shows a score drift right after the driver change — selector tie-breaks now prefer the vectorized path for some seq/batch shapes.

lina: could be warp scheduling or TensorCore microchanges. driver can change kernel latency profiles subtly.

ops-bot: Deploy event: driver-upgrade-54423 applied to h100-pool (region: us-west2) at 2026-03-16T10:45Z

sam: repro steps (local h100):
```bash
./perf_probe --model redwood-7b --seq 512 --batch 8 --profile --nvprof
```

maya: can we force a kernel family for now? e.g. export RW_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=aten_attn_generic or set model config kernel_hint.

jin: runtime accepts RW_KERNEL_HINT per model version. we can patch canary quickly.

lina: prefer that to a full driver rollback — faster and lower blast radius. set on prod-canary for 30m and observe.

sam: also noticed kv_cache batching decision changed: kv_cache_prefetch_threshold got effectively lower, producing smaller batches and worse throughput. need to snapshot kv/batching counters.

maya: immediate mitigation proposal:
- patch canary model config: kernel_hint=aten_attn_generic
- enable fallback policy: if p99 > baseline + 20ms for 5m -> force previous kernel selection
- collect 10 nvprof traces and full timeline traces for rootcause

deploy-bot: Canary update requested: redwood-7b@canary -> kernel_hint=aten_attn_generic (requested by maya)

jin: after forcing generic kernel, p99 dropped back to baseline within ~7m. looks promising.

maya: good. still we need root cause: driver likely changed kernel occupancy/latency ordering. autotuner should be driver-aware.

lina: short-term fix: include driver-version hash and sm_arch in the autotuner feature vector; add a small regularizer to prefer historically stable picks unless a new pick shows consistent wins across N samples.

sam: long-term: continuous kernel A/B with automatic rollback when regressions detected. we have rollout infra and metric bridge, we just need the autotune loop to act on it.

maya: I'll open a ticket with traces + sample metrics and tag eng-runtime + eng-runtime-ml. collecting nvprof outputs now.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0342 by maya (priority: P2)

jin: quick question — any memory footprint changes on the new kernel path? could affect kv cache batching thresholds.

maya: memcheck showed ~+0.2% device memory on the problematic kernel path. small but could nudge batching heuristics.

sam: ok planning: canary-wide sweep in next 2h. I'll coordinate the canary roll and metric checks.

lina: I'll sketch an autotuner PR to include driver/version and add a fallback gating signal. will post draft tonight.

maya: tagging @eng-runtime for visibility and follow-ups. thanks all.
